scenes.title: Say it clearly
scenes.sub: People judge service by how it was communicated
scenes.lead: Callers often judge service by how it was communicated, not only by the result. Aim to be understood, be respectful, and leave the person knowing what happens next.

scenes.heading: How we speak
scenes.lead: Five habits make a voice easy to trust.

items.goodSay: Say: Let me verify that for you.

items.good: "I will find the right person for that."
items.badSay: Instead of: That's not my department.
items.goodSay: Say: I will find the right person for that.

scenes.heading: Every message has five parts
scenes.lead: Every email and chat message has five parts, in this order.

scenes.heading: Set expectations
scenes.lead: Whenever you finish a conversation, explain three things.

scenes.title: Clarity over accent
scenes.sub: Lead with the answer. Be warm and direct.
scenes.lead: With callers in the United States, lead with the answer, and be warm and direct. Clarity matters more than accent. If you are unsure, check and restate.

scenes.title: Share only what is allowed
scenes.sub: Knowing when to say "I cannot share that"
scenes.lead: Families trust us with private information. Knowing when to say, I cannot share that, is as important as knowing what to say.

scenes.heading: Who am I speaking to?
scenes.lead: Before you discuss any details, confirm who the person is, and that they may have the information.

items.label: Only then share
items.say: Only then share what they may have.

scenes.title: A relationship is not authorization
scenes.sub: A friendly voice does not replace the check
scenes.lead: I am his sister. I am calling for my neighbour. These sound reasonable, and they are the most common way private information is shared by mistake. A friendly voice or a good reason does not replace the check.

scenes.heading: Private places, private messages
scenes.lead: Confidentiality is also about where and how you work.

items.text: Take calls where nobody can overhear
items.say: Take calls where nobody else can overhear.
No detailed messages on shared voicemail.

items.text: No caller talk on social media
items.say: No talking about callers on social media.

items.text: Close the case when you step away
items.say: And close the case when you step away.
We do not give medical advice.
Or financial advice, even when someone seems to need it.

scenes.title: Made a mistake? Say so
scenes.lead: If you make a mistake, tell your lead and report it straight away. Fast reporting limits harm. Reporting is never punished.

scenes.title: Heard first, helped second
scenes.sub: Patients, relatives and families of care-home residents
scenes.lead: Many of our calls come from patients, their relatives, and caregivers or family of people living in a care home. They need to be heard first and helped second.

scenes.heading: Our role and its limits
scenes.lead: We are not clinicians. We listen, verify, route and document.

items.text: Listen kindly and take the request
items.say: We listen and take the request.
Route it with a time frame.

items.text: Say what a symptom or result means
items.say: We never say what a symptom or result means.

items.label: Refills and records
items.say: Refills and records: route with a time frame.

items.label: Results worry
items.say: Results worry: listen, do not interpret, arrange a call from the care team.

items.label: Emergency
items.say: A possible emergency: follow the client's emergency steps.

scenes.heading: When it sounds urgent
scenes.lead: If a call sounds like an emergency, do not judge how serious it is. Act.

items.label: Call emergency services
items.say: Tell them to call emergency services.

items.label: Client's emergency steps
items.say: Follow the client's steps, and alert your lead.

items.label: Record it
items.say: And record the time, the words and what you said.

scenes.title: Safety comes first
scenes.sub: Each client's own steps are in its add-on module
scenes.lead: A routine request does not come first when a person's safety may be at risk. Never book, never wait, never reassure. Each client's own steps are taught in that client's add-on module.

scenes.title: Behavior is a signal
scenes.lead: Callers are not difficult people. They are people having a difficult time. What you hear usually points to something they need.

scenes.heading: What you hear, what they may need

items.label: Shouting
items.say: Shouting: to be heard, then a plan.

items.label: Same question again
items.say: The same question again: reassurance and a next step.

items.label: Demands
items.say: Demands: respect and a clear option.

items.label: Calls again and again
items.say: Calling again and again: a problem never solved.

items.text: Angry: let them vent, then steer to solving
items.say: Angry: let them vent briefly, then steer to solving.

items.text: Anxious: calm answers, a next step with a time
items.say: Anxious: answer calmly, with a next step and a time.

items.text: Confused: one step at a time
items.say: Confused: one step at a time, checking understanding.
Demanding: stay professional, and offer escalation.

scenes.title: Repeat callers
scenes.sub: Usually a problem that was never solved
scenes.lead: Callers who ring again and again usually have a problem that was never solved. Ask what is still open, then close the loop with a clear owner and time.

scenes.heading: Abuse and threats
scenes.lead: You do not have to accept being abused. If a caller uses threats or slurs:

items.label: End the call if it continues
items.say: If it continues, end the call, following your client's policy.

scenes.title: After a hard call
scenes.sub: Facts, not opinions. Then a short reset.
scenes.lead: After a hard call, write down the facts, not opinions, and take a short reset before the next call.
